source.author: verg
source.text: O luce magis dilecta sorori, solane perpetua maerens carpere iuventa, nec dulcis natos, Veneris nec praemia noris?
source.text_original: 'O luce magis dilecta sorori, / solane perpetua maerens carpere iuventa, / nec dulcis natos, Veneris nec praemia noris?
source.text_english: O sister, more dear than light, are you to remain alone, grieving through your endless youth, and know neither your sweet children nor the rewards of love?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: non suadent, quod tibi, sed, quod sibi prosit, et saepe illud obganniunt: solane perpetua maerens carpere iuuenta nec dulces natos Ueneris nec praemia noris?
reuse.text_original: non suadent, quod tibi, sed, quod sibi prosit, et saepe illud obganniunt: solane perpetua maerens carpere iuuenta nec dulces natos Ueneris nec praemia noris?
reuse.text_english: They do not advise what is good for you, but what is advantageous to themselves, and they are always yapping the same thing: Are you to continue forever in sorrow, and in your youth know neither the sweet children of Venus nor the rewards?
